segments.text: yadātu amyeva antarīm turya dāshām, atmati anivymrashcethi,
and on the contrary, when this internal state of turya is not concentrated
and is not maintained with awareness, always.
Then they hide the pramadrta bhavāt, then ego or ainess,
eye consciousness on body, eye consciousness on puristaka,
eye consciousness on prāna and shunya.
It's there and upurnam manyatātma kānaumal rupa,
then he feels himself as incomplete,
all around incomplete.
Then desire appears in him.
By the desire, abilāshāt, bhahirgati, samvāyāsya,
by the desire to fulfill his nature of being.
There is a gap.
He feels there is gap.
It must be filled.
So there is desire to fulfill it, fulfill that gap in him.
By that desire, bhahirgati,
his flow and his movement moves towards objective world
and not towards subjective consciousness.
Thus he becomes samvāyā.
Samvāyā means he becomes carried.
He is carried from one birth to another birth,
from one death to another death.
He is carried just like a beast.
Shakti chakra adistatai, carried by whom?
Carried by those energies which are established,
which have been established or governed by the
wheel of the supreme wheel of energies of God.
And those are kānchukā, antākarna, bhahiskarna, tanmaatr bhūtaisah.
Kānchukā, six coverings, kala vidyāra, kāl nitya, and māyā.
Antākarna, mind, intellect and ego.
Bhahiskarna, organs of actions and organs of senses.
Antākarna, five tānmātras, sound, shāvūtspur, rūpras and gun.
And by these, he is carried.
He is being carried from one state to another state,
from one life to another life.
What is that?
And the meaning is, yonir yon yandharam niyete.
From one womb, he is carried to another womb, by and by.
Thus he is somewhere here.
He is being carried.
He is not carrier.
He is carried.
In brief, he is kānmātmūrupa, pashū.
He is pashū just like a beast, dependent upon his past actions,
past and future actions.
Abhilaśo malotrato.
This is the māl.
Desire is māl.
Desire is dot, impurity.
Yatisri sācchandu okt nitya.
Upurnam manyata-atmaka abhiddhā kānmāla rūpāt.
Abhilaśāt hētor, bairgati.
By this coating of sācchanda, Upurnam manyata-atmaka abhiddhā kānmālaat.
That anamala which has appeared by Upurnam manyata, by considering,
by perceiving one's own self as incomplete.
And when you perceive yourself incomplete, that is aviddhā, that is ignorance.
And that ignorance is anamala.
And by that anamala, Abhilaśa desire rises in you.
And by that desire, bairgati, you are carried outside.
You are carried outside world, not internal world, of spirituality.
Hence, Vishion mokhattam eobavati.
So, your consciousness is diverted towards worldly pleasures.
Natu antermaka rūpā abhiddhā kānmāla rūpāt.
You cannot maintain.
He does not maintain awareness for establishing antermaka rūpā.
This, the nature of being introverted, being centralized in one's own nature.
That is lost.
It is said in Kalika krami.
Kalika kramśāstra also says the same thing.
Yet aviddhā vṛtata-tāyā, vikalpo vṛdiyogata,
shvādi nāyvijatiyati samudbāvīti ekhilaān.
When that ignorance covers that self by the way of vikalpo,
by the way of trading on vikalpā.
Then akhilaān shvādi nāyvijatiyati samudbāvīti.
It cannot perceive this whole universe beginning from earth to Shiva
as one with God consciousness.
He does not perceive like that.
He perceives differentiatedly in a differentiated manner.
Then what comes, what is the fruit of that?
Tata shubhā shubhā bāvā laksanti bāskāma.
Tata shubhā shubhā bāvā laksanti.
Then he becomes the object of two states, good and bad.
He becomes object of good and bad.
Tata shubhā tata-tāyā, by becoming object of good and bad,
asubhā bāvā laksanti bāvā laksanti,
he experiences in his own nature only pain.
And that pleasure also as being.
Atat-tāṁ kālpanāṁ kṛta-pachanti-narakāyatissu.
When your consciousness is established in that which is not real,
atat-tāṁ, that which is not real.
When your consciousness is established on that which is not real,
then pachanti-narakāyatissu.
You become object of nārak, health, not heaven.
Sothāyā dvośeśidāyanti vēno vainināyata.
It is just like the same thing just as by your own impurities
and your own drawbacks, your loss, your destroy.
You destroy yourself by your own drawbacks, just like vēno vainināyata.
Just like those bamboo trees, just like as they burn by their own fire.
That fire is produced in them and they burn by their own fire.
Yes. Maya, Maya, Seda, Baba, Ayuraviddhyam, Paribunjati, Maya, Maya, Tanum, Yanti, Tejara, Klesi, Baadhyana.
Those, those people who enjoy the nature of ignorance, not the nature of spirituality.
By adjusting in them, in their nature, those objects which are not beyond Maya, beyond illusion.
So, they become, they take the formation of Maya. Maya, Maya, Tanum, Yanti, Tejara, Klesi, Baadhyana.
In the end, they are Klesivajanam, they experience only Klesha, only pain, sadness.
